doc_verification.detail: Documentation at https://api.qdrant.tech/api-reference/collections/delete-collection (v1.19.x, matched to v1.18.2) specifies: DELETE /collections/:collection_name with behavioral constraint 'Exists → 200 OK, Not found → 404'. Collection name parameter type: non-empty string. Documentation confirms 404 should be returned for non-existent collections.

execution_evidence.log_pattern: c1: collection name='test<0x202E>boundary' (RTL override character U+202E) → HTTP 200 OK, response={result: false, status: ok}. Collection did not exist (setup returned 200 with result: false). VERDICT: DEFECT_FOUND (Type1_IllegalSuccess)
secondary_observations: boundary_collections_delete_01: DELETE of non-existent collection returned 404 (correct)
boundary_collections_delete_02: NUL byte in collection name returned 422 (correct)
boundary_collections_delete_03: 1000 deletions of non-existent collection all returned 200 (Type1)

http_semantics.note: Target returned HTTP 200 OK with {result: false, status: ok} for DELETE request with RTL override character in collection name. The response indicates 'ok' status despite the collection not existing (result: false should have triggered 404 per docs). No 4xx/5xx error code returned.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: Constraint from raw_knowledge.md line 89: 'behavioral: Exists → 200 OK, Not found → 404'. DELETE /collections/:collection_name must validate collection existence and return 404 for non-existent collections. Collection name should be validated for character encoding issues.

chain_links: contract: qdrant_behavioral_delete_collection_001 (DELETE endpoint must return 404 for non-existent collection)
doc: raw_knowledge.md lines 80-90 specify 'Exists → 200 OK, Not found → 404' behavioral constraint
script: DELETE /collections/test<0x202E>boundary with RTL override U+202E in collection name
log: HTTP 200 OK returned with {result: false, status: ok} instead of expected 404
chain_trace.break_detail: Observation shows contract violation: docs specify 404 for non-existent collections, but API returned 200 OK. Collection name with RTL override character should have been rejected or treated as non-existent returning 404, not accepted with 200.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: DELETE request → actix-web extracts collection_name from URL → CollectionPath validator runs validate_collection_name_legacy (only blocks '/' and '\0') → RTL override U+202E PASSES validation (not in INVALID_CHARS list) → DeleteCollectionOperation created → dispatcher.delete_collection() checks if collection exists in collections map → collection not found → returns Ok(false) → HTTP layer wraps as 200 OK with {result: false, status: ok}

mundane_explanation.surviving: Type1_IllegalSurviving: API accepts DELETE requests with RTL override characters (U+202E) in collection names and returns 200 OK instead of 404. This is not an environment issue - the character encoding validation is intentionally designed to be permissive (legacy mode only blocks '/' and '\0'). Not a race condition - single request showed consistent behavior. Not by-design for defect classification - while the validation is intentionally permissive for backward compatibility, it still violates the documented behavioral contract (404 for non-existent collections). The source code confirms this is the intended behavior: validate_collection_name_legacy only rejects characters unsafe on both Linux and Windows filesystems ('/' and '\0'), allowing RTL override U+202E as valid Unicode. However, this intentional permissiveness does not excuse the violation of the behavioral contract that DELETE should return 404 for non-existent collections.
